title: Configurable PIN length (4-6 digits)
description: Buried scope note from LODGY-4: PIN length was fixed at 4 digits since neither DESIGN.md nor the ticket specified one, and a variable-length flow needs an explicit confirm control the wireframe didn't show. Revisit if wardens want a longer PIN.
acceptanceCriteria: PIN setup supports a warden-chosen length between 4 and 6 digits
Setup flow has an explicit confirm step regardless of chosen length
Existing 4-digit PINs from before this change continue to work unchanged

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Starting - warden-chosen 4-6 digit PIN with an explicit confirm step. The stored bcrypt hash carries no length, so existing 4-digit PINs keep working without any migration; the lock screen just has to stop assuming 4.

PIN length is now the warden's choice, 4-6. AuthPreferences gained pinLength (MIN 4 / MAX 6 / DEFAULT 4, clamped on both read and write); the bcrypt hash carries no length of its own, so this preference is the only thing that has to remember, and an install from before this change has no stored value, reads 4, and unlocks exactly as it did - AC 3 needs no migration. Setup: length chips on the ENTER step (locked once the first digit is typed, so the dots can never disagree with what is being entered) and an explicit Continue / Confirm PIN button on both steps, replacing the old auto-advance-at-4-digits. That was forced anyway - with a variable length there is no digit count that reliably means 'done' - and it satisfies AC 2 directly. The chosen length is written on save. The lock screen keeps auto-verifying, but at the stored length rather than a hardcoded 4, and its dots follow it. Tests: PinSetupViewModelTest now drives the explicit submit, and covers the six-digit path with setPinLength persisted, a submit refused on an incomplete PIN, nothing advancing before the button, the length locking after the first digit, and the 4-6 option list; PinLockViewModelTest covers a six-digit unlock only firing on the sixth digit and the legacy four-digit install still unlocking. testDebugUnitTest green (309 tests).

PASS. AC1: the setup screen offers 4 / 5 / 6 digits and honours the choice - picked 6, entered a 6-digit PIN, and the dot indicator showed six positions. AC2: there is an explicit confirm step regardless of length - Continue moves to 'Confirm your PIN', and a deliberate mismatch was rejected with 'PINs didn't match - try again' and returned to the create step rather than silently accepting. AC3: existing 4-digit PINs are unaffected - AuthPreferences.pinLength falls back to DEFAULT_PIN_LENGTH (4) when the pin_length key is absent, which is exactly the state of a pre-change install, and the stored bcrypt hash format is untouched; AuthPreferencesTest asserts the unset-key default and PinLockViewModelTest covers both 4- and 6-digit unlock. End to end: force-stopped the app and unlocked with the 6-digit PIN across several restarts during this session.
